sections.title: Basic Concept of a Clock
sections.content:
A clock has 12 hours. The minute hand moves 360° in 60 minutes. The hour hand moves 360° in 12 hours.

Main Formula: Angle = |30H − 5.5M|
Where H = Hour, M = Minute

Example: At 3:00 → Angle = |30×3 − 5.5×0| = 90°

2–3 Step Method:
1. Put the values of H and M.
2. Substitute into the formula.
3. If the answer is more than 180°, subtract it from 360°.

sections.title: Special Angles of Clock Hands
sections.content:
A straight line (180°) is formed 22 times in a day.
A right angle (90°) is formed 44 times in a day.

Example: At 6:00 → Angle = 180° (straight line)

Logic: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours, therefore 22 times in 24 hours.

sections.title: Mirror and Water Image
sections.content:
Formula for Mirror Image: 11:60 − Given Time
For Water Image: 5:60 − Given Time (used as a mental trick)

Example: Mirror image of 3:20
11:60 − 3:20 = 8:40

Steps:
1. Write 11:60.
2. Subtract the given time.
3. The result will be the mirror time.

sections.title: Leap Year and Standard Year
sections.content:
Leap Year Rules:
1. A year divisible by 4 → Leap year
2. A century year (like 1900) is not a leap year
3. A century year divisible by 400 (like 2000) → Leap year

Examples:
1900 → Divisible by 100 but not by 400 → Not a leap year
2000 → Divisible by 400 → Leap year

A leap year has 366 days, a normal year has 365 days.

sections.title: Odd Days and Finding the Day
sections.content:
1 normal year = 1 odd day
1 leap year = 2 odd days

A week has 7 days, so divide by 7 and take the remainder.

Example:
If 10 March is Monday, then 17 March = 7 days later → It will also be Monday.

Steps:
1. Find the difference in days.
2. Divide by 7 and take the remainder.
3. Move forward according to the remainder.

sections.title: Finding the Day After Some Days/Months
sections.content:
Remember the number of days in months:
January 31, February 28/29, March 31, April 30...

Example:
If 1 April is Tuesday, then 11 April = 10 days later
10 ÷ 7 = remainder 3
Tuesday + 3 days = Friday

2–3 Step Method:
1. Add total days.
2. Divide by 7.
3. Move days according to the remainder.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content:
Main Formula: |30H − 5.5M|
Leap year: Divisible by 4, check 400 rule for century years.
Odd day logic: Take the remainder of total days ÷ 7.
Mirror image: 11:60 − Time.
Straight line: 22 times, Right angle: 44 times.

tricks.title: Find Angle Instantly
tricks.explanation: Assume 30° per hour and 5.5° per minute effect.

tricks.title: Angle Greater than 180°
tricks.explanation: If the answer is greater than 180°, subtract it from 360°.

tricks.title: Leap Year Shortcut
tricks.explanation: Just check divisibility by 4, but always verify the 400 rule for century years.

tricks.title: Century Year Trick
tricks.explanation: 1900 is not a leap year, but 2000 is because it is divisible by 400.

tricks.title: Find Odd Day Quickly
tricks.explanation: Divide the difference in days by 7; the remainder is what matters.
tricks.example: After 15 days → 15 ÷ 7 = remainder 1 → Move 1 day ahead

tricks.title: Water Image Trick
tricks.explanation: Use the mental trick of subtracting the time from 5:60.

tricks.title: Remember Straight Line
tricks.explanation: 11 times in 12 hours, 22 times in 24 hours.

tricks.title: Remember Right Angle
tricks.explanation: A 90° angle forms 44 times in a day.

tricks.title: 7-Day Cycle
tricks.explanation: Every 7 days the same day repeats.
